units: degrees (COG stores Int16 tenths of a degree: value / 10 = degrees)
source: MOLA/HRSC blended DEM, 200 m/px (Mars_HRSC_MOLA_BlendDEM_Global_200mp_v2, USGS Astrogeology)

method.corridor: habitat (-176.05, 45.97) + 4 POIs from sites.geojson, buffered 20 km
method.slope_grid: local equirectangular metre grid, +proj=eqc +lat_ts=45.5 +lon_0=183.21138698297565 +R=3396190 +units=m +no_defs, 200 m, bilinear
method.algorithm: gdaldem slope (Horn 3×3), then bilinear back to lon/lat at the source resolution

caveats: 200 m cells average out short steep slopes (crater walls, scarps, ridges narrower than a few hundred metres): use for drive-leg routing only, never for the final approach or the walking leg (use the 1 m HiRISE slope there).
Real local slopes are steeper than this layer shows; treat a 200 m slope near the limit as a likely hazard.
The slope threshold (20°, config.yaml slope_max_deg) is the suit/walking limit. The agreed rover limits (5° caution, 10° no-go) apply to the router's 463 m MOLA grid, not to this 200 m layer.
The blended DEM is MOLA-only where HRSC has no coverage, so effective resolution can be coarser than 200 m between MOLA tracks.
Local metre grid is true-scale at 45.5°N; east-west distances are off by ≤ ~3 % at the corridor's north/south edges.
